operator_statement.text: it's usual s0101 arm ask internet. No spacer
operator_statement.interpretation: Operator attests standard SO101 and no spacer between base and table. This does not measure manufactured part dimensions or joint zero.

method.support: Compile the pinned native XML alone at q=0. Transform each base-body visual mesh vertex and triangle into the base frame. Count vertices/faces within 1 micrometre of each mesh minimum z, compute coplanar face area and footprint.
method.scan: For each placement, change only the fixed base body world z in memory; preserve table, recorded mapping, native meshes/limits/collision masks. Run mj_forward on every second recorded observation row, scan all in-limit poses using existing geometry-collision contact rules. No dynamics, fitting, clipping, asset edits or production configuration edits. Task-relative observations/camera transforms are not evaluated by this isolated contact comparison.

nominal_no_spacer_candidate.why_not_zero: The native base frame is 2.4 mm above the broad bottom support face. Setting base_z_offset=0 places that physical support face 2.4 mm below the tabletop.
nominal_no_spacer_candidate.why_not_legacy: The provisional +12 mm base origin leaves the native base support face 9.6 mm above the table despite the operator reporting no spacer.
nominal_no_spacer_candidate.confidence: Geometrically justified placement of the pinned standard CAD, conditional on user standard-part/no-spacer statement; not independent metrology of the real printed part.

conclusions: Use nominal +2.4 mm native base-origin height for a separately versioned no-spacer candidate, not 0 mm.
Correcting the unsupported lift increases table penetration; it is a geometry correction, not a collision workaround or evidence that joint mapping agrees.
Rigid base translation cannot repair arm self-collisions or recorded native joint-limit violations.
The support conclusion comes from a broad coplanar downward-facing base surface, not an isolated minimum vertex.
Re-register camera/table/object coordinates coherently before using this candidate for images or policy evaluation; in-memory scan changes robot height alone intentionally.
